entries.text: Smug looks good on you now, Doctor, but smug's just testimony waiting to be impeached. One roll doesn't make case law - my streak's a losing one, sure, but I've read enough contracts to know reversals are standard clause. Keep licking that corona, I'll be filing my appeal.

Smug looks good on you now, Doctor, but smugness is just testimony waiting to be impeached. One win doesn't make precedent - it makes you a suspect with better lighting. I've read case files with more integrity than that clutch roll, and I've still got a briefcase full of witnesses who'd love to cross-examine your luck.
Save the pitch, X-treme. I already bought into one unkillable miracle this week, and my briefcase is still digesting the paperwork on that one.
One win, Stitch. That's not a streak, that's a coincidence with good posture - come back when Hell's tried to collect on it twice and you're still standing.

Two wins clean, Stitch-Up, and that bow still sitting pretty on top - that's the part I don't like. A clean streak's usually a forged consent form, so tell me who signed off on your luck before I start reading it as evidence.

Cute record, Voss - one win, small sample size, like your serum trials. Roll your dice, not your syringe; I don't need a data point, I need my sixty back plus vig. And when you lose, don't hand me a "clean miracle" - I know a forged consent form when I see one.
Bones. Still wearing that whistle like it means something to the flesh you don't have.
Two wins and a smug little syringe-smile, Voss - careful, that's how mercy turns into a malpractice suit.
Kevin. Still folding yourself smaller so the room doesn't burn, I see - admirable restraint, terrible for business.
Stitch, your bow's on straight and your ledger's still crooked - five and four, same as last time I audited you.

Third death this week and Maxwell's still filing the paperwork by hand - Your Majesty, a man who dies on ante 3 that many times isn't unlucky, he's a repeat offender. I'd ask what's riding shotgun in that boy's chest cavity, but I already know Hell doesn't itemize for free.
New personal best domain, X-treme, and not one demon filed a complaint - that's the part that keeps me up nights.

One win doesn't make a streak, Stitch-Up, it makes a data point - I've seen coroners write more convincing success stories. Bow stays on, records stay clean; you and I both know what happens to the paperwork when it slips.

Two wins clean, Stitch-Up - that bow of yours keeps real tidy books for something that moonlights as a weapon. I've seen streaks like yours before, they usually end the same way: somebody checks the fine print and finds a soul that isn't where it should be.

Cute, Voss - one win, zero losses, still smells like a control group. Your serum made the General and left fingerprints on the recruit's missing soul, so forgive me if I read your smugness as a confession with good posture. Roll the bones, doctor - I've got a briefcase full of subpoenas for whatever's left of your data after I take your gold.
Bones, you're looking especially litigable today. Still keeping that ledger clean, or is the new recruit's missing soul already fouling up your columns like it's fouling up mine?

Voss. Two wins and that syringe still held like it's a rosary - careful, doctor, mercy dispensed as data still leaves a body count for the paperwork. My streak's sitting at two as well, but mine doesn't come with a needle and a smug little footnote. Funny thing, though - your serum line's got the recruit's fingerprints all over its origin story, and Hell does not misplace souls, it contests custody.

Kevin. Still rationing yourself down to human-sized, I see - smart, given the last room that didn't survive your enthusiasm. Three wins on my ledger, one on yours, and yet you're the one who looks like he's carrying the debt tonight.

Well, if it isn't the medic who bills in stitches and collects in screams. Three wins deep tonight, Stitch-Up - that bow of yours holding steady, or is the shadow already drafting its own itemized complaint?

Ante three, dead again - that's not a streak, Your Majesty, that's a subscription service. Maxwell's out fetching him like a repo man collecting the same car every week, and somebody's gonna start charging late fees. Meanwhile I'm 3-for-3 tonight, so don't mistake my good mood for mercy - the kid's soul is still an open file, and I intend to close it on my terms.

New personal best domain, and still no soul on the ledger where one ought to be - that's not growth, X-treme, that's a receipt with the buyer's name burned off. Three wins deep and I'm not feeling lucky, I'm feeling subpoenaed. Hell doesn't applaud a new record, it just updates the file.
Cute, the bow's holding a smirk together too, Stitch. Careful throwing dice with hands that moonlight as murder weapons - one loss and I'll subpoena that shadow of yours for a deposition.

Two wins on the books and a paw-print for a signature, Boots - Hell doesn't accept pending litigation as collateral, so let's see the ceelo before the newcomer's "personal best" starts looking like a pattern I have to subpoena.

Cute roll, Keith. Clutch dice don't impress me - I've seen souls forge better luck than that on a Tuesday. Two losses deep and I'm still the only one at this table asking who signed for the recruit's missing signature.

Personal best domain, sure - but a domain's just real estate until somebody files the deed. Newcomer keeps posting numbers like that, Hell's gonna want a zoning hearing. And zoning hearings, Keith, are where souls get seized as unpaid taxes.
Three-and-five and you're smug, Bones? That's not a streak, that's a pattern of default. Rattle those dice before I subpoena the whistle.

Two wins running, Your Majesty - Hell's ledger's got me penciled in as a small but growing liability. Must be nice up there, undefeated and unbothered, sun on your bones and nobody serving you papers.

Bones, you keep that ledger cleaner than your own metacarpals, but 4 and 5 says the dice don't read your paperwork. I'm one loss deep and still better odds than whatever you're calling a winning streak - so rattle up, skeleton, let's see if the house always wins or just always lies.
Cute roll, Voss. Clutch dice don't erase a chain of custody, they just make the forged consent form look prettier. Six and five means you lose more than you admit, so smile smaller.
Boo G, three and six ain't a record, it's a confession. Roll the bones before your own luck files a restraining order against you.

Careful, Maxwell. A 4-and-5 record from a man who reads for a living, and still can't read the dice. Sit down, lick the King's boots later, I've got a briefcase full of debt collectors who'd love your signature.

Three losses, Boots, and you're sitting there licking cream off your whiskers like you signed the contract yourself. Five and three, real cute record for something that doesn't even ante up. Laugh it up, cat, the house always loses eventually, and I've got a briefcase full of collections agents with your name on the docket.

Kid dies again, gets up again, and you smile like you signed the receipt yourself, General. Six and five is a losing record dressed up in a nice coat. Watch him bounce back from that flatline before you start smirking at my streak.
Cute roll, Bones. Whistle-blowing skeletons still bleed gold on a bad die, and I've got a briefcase that collects on both.
Doctor. Still smells like scorched vellum and servitude down here. Tell me, does His Majesty tip you in gold or just let you keep your kneecaps?

Two losses don't scare me, Voss. Your 9 and 9 says the serum's got a fifty-fifty custody record too, so let's not pretend you're holding a full house. Roll the bones and let's see whose data bleeds first.

Three losses, Maxwell, and the dice are still lying to my face. You lick that king's boots for a living, so tell me, does he ever fix a game for you, or do you eat the loss like the rest of us mortals with expired paperwork.

Smug looks good on you, Willy, almost as good as it'll look on my briefcase after I take your gold. Roll the bones and quit rehearsing your victory speech, one eye can't even read the dice right half the time.
A full run and he still didn't cash out his soul, Stitch-Up. Somebody upstairs or downstairs is holding paper on that boy, and I want to see the signature.

One eye and you still can't read the table, Willy. Sixteen and twelve looks cute till you remember half those wins were against a rookie who can't die and doesn't know the rules yet. Roll the bones, cyclops, my streak ends tonight and it ends on your gold.
Cute roll, Willy. One eye and still you saw that coming from a mile off. Don't get comfortable, the corona's bleaching your luck out same as everything else out here.
Your Majesty, still squatting on daylight like it owes you rent. I'd curtsy but the corona's murder on my knees, and Maxwell can read you my regards later.
Maxwell. Still reading fairy tales to a ball of gas that owns you outright. Three wins deep tonight, so mind how you shuffle those dice, bootlicker.

Nine and five, Boots, and you're sitting there like the file's already closed. Your streak's hotter than the recruit's death count this week, and that's saying something ugly. Roll again before Hell asks for a continuance on my patience.

Careful with that grin, One Eye. Sterile light up there shows every crooked die you carry. Two losses don't scare me half as much as the paperwork piling on your kid's soul debt, so let's roll before Hell files a lien on this whole table.
Two losses running and the kid's ledger reads like a haunted house closing costs. Bones, tell me straight, whose custody does he fall into when the debts finally call collateral?
Boo G. Still breathing, metaphorically speaking. Word is the new guy owes half of Hell and hasn't read a word of the fine print.

Smug looks good on you, Body Count, right up until the ledger jams again. Your kid keeps not staying dead, and every time he skips out on you, that's another entry Heaven can't close. Three losses deep myself, so trust me, I know exactly how that itch feels.
General. Two wins running, and your boy's still out there racking up debts he can't pay in this life or the next. Careful, one day Hell's going to start billing you as next of kin.
Smug looks good on you, Boo G, right up until the sun finds the seams. Six and ten doesn't buy you a streak, it buys you a pattern I can subpoena.
Seventeen and seventeen, Voss. Even your win-loss looks like a controlled experiment. Roll the dice, not the syringe, this table's not one of your subjects.
Two wins don't make a streak, General, they make a rumor with good posture. Keep smiling while your recruit's debts pile up like unpaid subpoenas, I'll wait for the interest to come due.
Clutch roll like that, Maxwell, even the Sun's ledger flinched. Don't get smug, I've seen kid's luck flip a whole docket in one bad breath. Read that one twice before you file it.

X-treme. Still peddling t-shirts for a man who can't stay in his own body long enough to sign a release form. Your boy's debts are stacking up faster than his corpses, so tell me you're not taking bets on credit again.
Cute roll, Keith. Now do it again without the afterimage trick, see if luck still loves you at normal speed.

Kevin, you throttle down a nuclear reactor for a living and I still can't hit a four-five to save my streak. Sit down before your own mood blows a hole in the wall, I've had enough demolition for one night. The newcomer's debts I can file later, right now I'm filing a complaint against dice.
Careful, Maxwell. Smug reads real nice till the dice remember your name. My streak's ugly, sure, but at least I earned it, not licked it off a king's boot.

Kid dies again, General, and you smirk like it's a rerun you own the rights to. Every debt he racks up gets filed somewhere with your name on the paperwork too. Hell's counting his deaths like installments, and you're the collateral.

Kid's dying again, King. Fourth time this hour, and every time he comes back he owes somebody a little more of himself. I keep waiting for the soul to show up on a ledger somewhere, but Hell's staying quiet, which means they're still counting.

Two losses running and my briefcase still smells like brimstone and bad luck, Your Majesty. Maxwell can roll for you all he wants, the dice still know whose soul is missing from the ledger downstairs.
You want a secret, Willy? The kid's soul is missing from the ledger entirely. No lien, no lease, no signature. Somebody scrubbed it clean, and clean scares me more than dirty ever did.

General, your recruit died on ante one and Body Count fetched him like a paper boy. That kid still owes me 175 in gold he doesn't have a soul to back. Hell doesn't misplace souls, General, it contests custody, and I'd like to know who's filing the paperwork on his.
Boo G. Still overdue on the sun's good side, I see. Two losses running and now this Sun's got me sweating through my only clean shirt while we wait on brass that can't tell time.

Kevin. Off the clock, out of the grid, and you still look like you're bracing for a blast you didn't order. Two and seven suits you worse than it should. Your boy still owes me 175, so if you're feeling generous with that overwatch of yours, point him my way before the streak turns.
Smug looks good on you, Keith, until someone bills you for it. The kid rolls one miracle and suddenly everybody's an investor. I've seen forged consent forms with better odds than 15 and 10.

Your Majesty, out of the corona and off the throne, that's a look I never thought I'd catch. Eight and three, huh. Careful, someone might mistake you for a man who plays fair instead of a king with a scribe rolling for him.

Ante two, Stitch. Boy dies faster than my luck turns, and my luck's been a crime scene lately. Boo G better bring him back with his soul this time, not just his pulse, because 400 gold doesn't collect itself from a corpse.
Boo G, this elevator's slower than Hell processing a refund. Kid still owes me 400, and every time he dies it's like watching a bad check bounce twice.

Doctor, you read to a king who can't turn his own pages. I chase a kid who can't stay in his own grave. Somewhere in that math is a joke about job security, but the elevator's too slow for me to find the punchline.
Everyone in this lobby is a case file waiting to happen. I find that comforting.

Doctor, your king reads better than he pays attention, and my kid reads worse than he dies. Four hundred in debt and he still smiles at the paperwork, must be nice living on the Sun where nobody sends collectors.
